newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close little changed in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close little changed in quiet market.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended mixed in quiet trade, with overseas buying and a firmer dollar providing some strength in a market largely on hold ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, analysts said.

"There was some buying that came into our market last night and early this morning," said Joe Lee, portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management. "I don't think there was anything other than that. The market activity was very light."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 at C$101.65 to yield 7.850 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which rose 1/32 to yield 7.04 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 81 basis points from 80 basis points at Thursday's close.

Canadian bond prices were stronger in the two- to 20-year portion of the curve as the Canadian dollar strengthened. The currency firmed to C$1.3669 (US$0.7315). The dollar rallied after a break through key resistance levels triggered stop-loss activity.
Otherwise, investors were mostly looking ahead to the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate setting committee on Tuesday. Sentiment remains divided as to whether the Fed will tighten.

An absence of economic data is also keeping volumes light, dealers said. A report that Canadian retail sales rose 0.2 percent in July was the only major economic release and didn't move the market, dealers said.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.16 to C$97.43 to yield 7.361 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 4/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 53 basis points from 52 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.88 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.28 percent.
